Subject: Patient image uploads & BAA question

Hi Tessa,

Quick intro — I’m Amy (Head of Security/Privacy at HealthPro Pharmacy). We’re evaluating a feature where patients upload prescription photos and short notes through a portal. The vendor we're piloting with (you) would receive the images and pass text extracted from them to an LLM to summarize and flag potential errors before human review.

Before we get too far, can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood will consider this workload HIPAA-eligible, 2) if Redwood can sign a BAA, and 3) what PHI processing boundaries look like for the hosted API vs. Dedicated/Private deployments? We also need a high-level architecture diagram and any DPIA artifacts or evidence you can share.

We’re on a tight timeline — aiming for vendor security sign-off by 8/20. Can we schedule a 30-minute call this week?

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Reed
Head of Security & Privacy
HealthPro Pharmacy

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Patient image uploads & BAA question

Hi Amy — thanks for the clear summary and timeline. Short answers up front: 1) The hosted public API (default) is not HIPAA-eligible and we do not enter BAAs for hosted shared-tenancy endpoints. 2) We do sign BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments where the customer has isolation and required controls. 3) PHI boundary: patient images are considered PHI if they contain identifiers; we recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment when raw images or OCR results contain identifiers.

I’m looping in Rishi (account lead) to coordinate commercial options and Mina from Security to confirm evidence we can provide (DPIA, architecture diagram, SOC 2 attachments). Can you share a brief list of what you define as PHI in your flow (e.g., full name, DOB, patient ID, prescription details)? That will help us scope the DPIA items.

I can do a 30-min call on Thu 8/13 at 10am PT — does that work?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

PHI scope for our pilot: patient full name, DOB, prescription NDC codes, patient account ID, and uploaded photos (which sometimes include labels with name/phone). We plan to OCR the images and pass extracted text + a redacted image hash to the inference layer. Key asks before call:

Subject: Re: Patient image uploads & BAA question — architecture and next steps

Amy — follow-up from our call and next steps:

Summary: Dedicated deployment is the recommended path. Confirmed items:
- BAA: yes, Redwood can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. Link to DocuSign draft: https://docusign.net/HealthPro-BAA-12345
- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS and BYOK workflows) for encryption-at-rest of model weights and request logs.
- Audit logs: We provide request-level audit logs with configurable retention; for Dedicated we can expose a secure S3 bucket or push logs into your Splunk/Datadog instance.
- DPIA/artifacts: Attached is a high-level architecture diagram (patient-upload-arch-diagram.png) and a redacted DPIA example for image processing. For the DPIA we’ll need a short questionnaire from you about retention and de-id rules to finalize.

Next steps:
1) You sign the BAA draft via DocuSign (link above).
2) HealthPro to confirm retention windows and whether images are stored post-OCR.
3) Redwood to prepare Dedicated deployment onboarding plan and security checklist (we can begin provisioning once contract is executed).

We’ve attached the architecture diagram and the current BAA draft (redacted). If you want, Mina can follow up separately with personnel who will handle the DPIA details.

Best,
Tessa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
